item.title: We apologise if any of our messaging over the past days has created confusion. For the sake of clarity:
item.content:encoded: We apologise if any of our messaging over the past days has created confusion. For the sake of clarity:1. KDE is open, diverse and accepting and we have the track record to prove it. Please come join us and see for yourself.2. KDE does not harbor "fascists" and we have the track record to prove it.3. We are not writing a set of "pro-LLM" policies. Quite the contrary. The current draft actually restricts its use much more than currently codified.

VLC 3.0.24 is out.
item.content:encoded: This is mainly a security/maintenance release: 130+ security fixes across VLC and bundled libraries (the most we've ever handled) with LLM-assisted research likely contributing to the volume.Also: 49 third-party libraries updated, FFmpeg 4.4 → 8.1.2, support for CEA-708 in MP4, ATRAC3/9, SRT listener mode, and a new RSA-4096 update key.Still supports XP → 11, macOS 10.7 → current, Linux/BSD/OS/2.Thanks to the Sovereign Tech Fund supporting us!

item.title: #TDE[1]'s konsole now supports bracketed paste mode, like most other terminal emulators do. This means that unless you have some custom settings, copying text into Konsole command line will now result in the text being highlighted in inverted colors and waiting for "Enter" to be pressed. This allows multiline commands to be pasted as a block instead of each line being immediately executed during the pasting operation.

item.title: Software Freedom Day 2026: What Freedoms Does Libreoffice Offer
item.content:encoded: Software Freedom Day 2026: What Freedoms Does Libreoffice OfferToday, 19 September, is Software Freedom Day, a special day that the free software community celebrates every year on the third Saturday in September all over the world.It is a good opportunity to look at LibreOffice from a perspective that is often taken for granted: not what the software does, but what it allows users to do and what it does not impose on them.

item.title: It will be far easier for us to support upcoming Motorola devices than Pixels. Qualcomm will hopefully expand MTE support beyond the highest end flagship SoC soon so we can expand to more than flagships. Pixel 11 didn't remove it from hardware, only firmware, so that's good news.
item.content:encoded: It will be far easier for us to support upcoming Motorola devices than Pixels. Qualcomm will hopefully expand MTE support beyond the highest end flagship SoC soon so we can expand to more than flagships. Pixel 11 didn't remove it from hardware, only firmware, so that's good news.
